primitives.assumptions: Player follow relationships are static at time of transition; social ties reflect pre-transition relationships.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When p has no Twitter handle or no followers on team t.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that player transitions in professional sports can be modeled as a group transition problem, where social ties—captured through Twitter follow graphs—provide additional predictive signal beyond traditional metrics like salary and team rank. The primitive 'social_affinity_count' defines a kernel-based measure of how many players a given individual follows who are already on a candidate team. This count is then used as a feature in a probabilistic classifier that estimates the likelihood of a player moving to a specific team. The classifier operates under the assumption that the follow graph snapshot at the time of transition reflects meaningful pre-existing social relationships. However, this approach suffers from data leakage if the graph includes post-transition activity. To mitigate this, the 'temporal_point_in_time_graph' primitive ensures that only social structures known before the transition are used. The 'transition_probability_classifier' integrates both social and non-social features into a unified framework, enabling probabilistic predictions of team destinations. The failure mode arises when the model assumes independence among observations or when the dataset lacks sufficient temporal resolution to distinguish pre- from post-transition behavior.
